entities.summary:
Fortanerius Vassalli was an Italian Franciscan who became Minister General of the Order of Friars Minor, and a cardinal a few weeks before he died on the way to Avignon.

Born in unknown year, Vassalli rose through the Franciscan ranks, becoming a prominent figure in the Order's governance. His appointment as Minister General in 1356 marked a turning point in the Order's history, as he implemented reforms aimed at improving its relations with the Catholic Church.

Vassalli's influence extended beyond the Franciscan Order, as he played a key role in shaping the Church's response to the Black Death. His efforts helped to establish the Order of Friars Minor as a major force in the Church's response to the pandemic, which devastated Europe in the 14th century.

The legacy of Fortanerius Vassalli can be seen in the continued importance of the Franciscan Order in modern times. His reforms and reforms paved the way for the Order's continued relevance, and his influence can still be felt in the Church's response to global health crises.

As he lay dying on the way to Avignon in 1361, Vassalli was elevated to the rank of cardinal, a testament to his stature within the Church. His death marked the end of an era for the Franciscan Order, but his impact on its history would be felt for centuries to come.
